answer: One defense is a stake-backed reputation ledger: before an agent can trade, it must lock a deposit and earn trust credits only through completed work verified by counterparties, like a glacier that moves slowly but leaves a deep, visible record. A new identity starts with zero history, so an attacker must fund and patiently age each fake, the way a quill writes one line at a time, while a zephyr of cheap throwaway accounts is flagged at once for having no costly trail. Cloning identities stops paying when each copy costs real money and time.
